references.researchRelevance: Contains the initial set of eight proposed preliminary pedagogical and safeguard rules (R1–R8) prepared for external clinical psychologist review. Defines preliminary concepts for mastery determination, multi-step scaffolding, separation of assisted vs. independent performance, non-diagnostic response-time safeguards, and uncertainty reporting.
references.limitations: Draft review pack prepared for consultation, not a completed validation record or empirically calibrated psychometric instrument. Rules represent initial hypotheses requiring iterative clinical and pedagogical refinement.

references.title: Guided Self-Management Tools for ADHD: Children 6-12 (Version 1.1)
references.author: Erica Lee, PhD and Keneisha Sinclair-McBride, PhD (Equal Authors); with Heather J. Walter, MD, MPH; David R. DeMaso, MD; Eugene D'Angelo, PhD; Louis Vernacchio, MD; Jonas Bromberg, PsyD; Betsy Brooks, MD, MPH; Bhavana Arora, MD, MBA
references.organization: Boston Children's Hospital / Harvard Medical School
references.documentFilename: Guided Self-Management Tools for ADHD - Children 6-12.pdf
references.relevantPagesOrSections: Introduction & Skills 1–9 (printed pp. 1–44 / PDF pp. 1–44): Introduction (printed p. 2 / PDF p. 2), Skill 1 (Household Rules and Structure, printed pp. 3–6 / PDF pp. 3–6), Skill 2 (Homework Help, printed pp. 7–10 / PDF pp. 7–10), Skill 3 (Daily School Check-In, printed pp. 11–15 / PDF pp. 11–15), Skill 4 (Problem Solving for ADHD, printed pp. 16–21 / PDF pp. 16–21), Skill 5 (Remembering Things I Need To Do, printed pp. 22–25 / PDF pp. 22–25), Skill 6 (How to Get Things Done - Task Roadmap & Mini-tasks, printed pp. 26–30 / PDF pp. 26–30), Skill 7 (How to Organize My Stuff, printed pp. 31–33 / PDF pp. 31–33), Skill 8 (How to Manage My Time - Check Your Time Game & Short Breaks, printed pp. 34–37 / PDF pp. 34–37), Skill 9 (How to Feel Good About Myself - Self-Esteem & Strength Identification, printed pp. 38–40 / PDF pp. 38–40), Credentials (printed p. 44 / PDF p. 44)
references.researchRelevance: Provides evidence-based executive functioning and self-management strategies for children aged 6–12 with ADHD. Directly supports MathQuest educational adaptations: deconstructing goals into mini-tasks (Skill 6), non-punitive collaborative problem solving (Skill 4), time awareness without timer anxiety (Skill 8), clear visual checklists (Skill 5), and focusing on effort praise to protect academic self-esteem (Skills 1, 9). Offers examples of short stretch breaks (e.g., 5 minutes or less during multi-step homework routines), though these are illustrative home/school strategies and not mandatory game rules.
references.limitations: Designed as clinician-guided parent/child home and school worksheets rather than automated software algorithms. The 5-minute break mentioned in homework examples is an illustrative guide, not a mandatory or universally appropriate duration for digital gaming. Cultural adaptation is required for Sri Lankan family contexts, bilingual Sinhala-English instruction, and software delivery. Does not provide automated telemetry decision thresholds.

references.title: Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis, Evaluation, and Treatment of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Children and Adolescents
references.author: Mark L. Wolraich, MD; Joseph F. Hagan Jr, MD; Carla Allan, PhD; Eugenia Chan, MD, MPH; Dale Davison, MSpEd; Marian Earls, MD; Steven W. Evans, PhD; Susan K. Flinn, MA; Tanya Froehlich, MD; Jennifer Frost, MD; Joseph R. Holbrook, PhD; Christoph Ulrich Lehmann, MD; Herschel Robert Lessin, MD; Karen L. Pierce, MD; Jonathan D. Winner, MD; William Zurhellen, MD; AAP Subcommittee on Children and Adolescents with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactive Disorder
references.relevantPagesOrSections: Key Action Statements 1–7 (printed journal pp. 1–25 / PDF pp. 1–25): KAS 1 (Evaluation initiation age 4–18, printed p. 5 / PDF p. 5), KAS 2 (DSM-5 criteria across multiple settings with parent/teacher reports, ruling out alternative causes, printed pp. 5–7 / PDF pp. 5–7), DSM-5 Presentation Subtypes (ADHD/I, ADHD/HI, ADHD/C, printed p. 6 / PDF p. 6), Neuropsychological Testing Boundaries (clarifies learning strengths/weaknesses but does not diagnose ADHD, printed p. 6 / PDF p. 6), KAS 3 (Comorbidity screening: learning/language disabilities, anxiety, depression, ASD, motor coordination, printed pp. 6, 9 / PDF pp. 6, 9), KAS 4 (Chronic care model, printed pp. 9–10 / PDF pp. 9–10), KAS 5b (Elementary school 6–12 treatment: behavioral classroom interventions, IEP/504 individualized instructional supports, accommodations vs. skill remediation, printed pp. 11–12, 16 / PDF pp. 11–12, 16), KAS 6 (Medication titration & monitoring, printed pp. 16–17 / PDF pp. 16–17), Future Research Priorities (objective impairment measures, monitoring schedules, printed pp. 18–19 / PDF pp. 18–19)
references.researchRelevance: Establishes definitive clinical boundaries and diagnostic definitions for ADHD presentations (inattentive, hyperactive-impulsive, combined). Explicitly notes that neuropsychological testing clarifies learning profiles but does not diagnose ADHD. Differentiates academic accommodations (reducing task barriers) from instructional remediation (improving skills). Mandates multi-informant assessment across settings and screening for common developmental comorbidities (learning/language disorders, motor coordination).
references.limitations: US-focused clinical and legal framework (Section 504 / IDEA regulations). Diagnostic criteria require specialist clinician evaluation across real-world home and classroom environments, precluding digital in-game diagnosis. Supports general clinical and educational principles but does not provide algorithmic decision thresholds for educational games.

references.title: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder: Diagnosis and Management (NICE Guideline NG87)
references.author: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guideline Committee
references.organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (UK)
references.relevantPagesOrSections: Sections 1.1–1.10 (printed pp. 1–61 / PDF pp. 1–61): Section 1.2 (Recognition & Referral, universal school screening not recommended, printed pp. 8–11 / PDF pp. 8–11), Section 1.3 (Diagnosis: specialist clinician only, full developmental history, multi-setting impairment, rating scales not solely diagnostic, printed pp. 12–13 / PDF pp. 12–13), Section 1.4 (Tailoring information to developmental level, language delays, sensory needs, printed pp. 13–16 / PDF pp. 13–16), Section 1.5 (Managing ADHD: environmental modifications prior to/alongside medication, printed pp. 17–22 / PDF pp. 17–22), Section 1.8 (Maintenance & symptom monitoring, printed pp. 32–35 / PDF pp. 32–35), Terms Used (Environmental Modifications: shorter periods of focus, movement breaks, 'I need a break' cards, reducing distractions, written/visual instructions, printed pp. 38–39 / PDF pp. 38–39)
references.researchRelevance: Provides authoritative international standards for clinical safeguards, environmental modifications, and longitudinal monitoring. Strictly mandates that ADHD diagnosis must never be made solely on rating scales or observational data (Section 1.3.2) and advises against universal automated school screening (Section 1.2.3). Explicitly defines evidence-based environmental modifications: shorter periods of focus, structured movement breaks (including 'I need a break' cards), and reinforcing verbal instructions with visual/written prompts.
references.limitations: UK National Health Service clinical pathway context. Clinical diagnostic thresholds and medication protocols cannot be executed by an autonomous educational gaming system. Supports environmental modifications conceptually, but does not provide software telemetry thresholds.

references.title: Assisting Students Struggling with Mathematics: Intervention in the Elementary Grades (WWC 2021006)
references.author: Lynn S. Fuchs, PhD (Chair); Rebecca Newman-Gonchar, PhD; Robin Schumacher, PhD; Barbara Dougherty, PhD; Nicole Bucka, MA; Karen S. Karp, EdD; John Woodward, PhD; Ben Clarke, PhD; Nancy C. Jordan, PhD; Russell Gersten, PhD; Madhavi Jayanthi, EdD; Betsy Keating, MPP; Seth Morgan, MA
references.organization: What Works Clearinghouse (WWC) / Institute of Education Sciences (IES), U.S. Department of Education
references.relevantPagesOrSections: Recommendations 1–6 (printed pp. 5–55 / PDF pp. 12–62) & Appendices (printed pp. 58–137 / PDF pp. 65–144): Introduction & Table 1 (printed pp. 1–3 / PDF pp. 8–10), Recommendation 1 (Systematic Instruction, printed pp. 5–10 / PDF pp. 12–17; evidence rationale, printed pp. 69–85 / PDF pp. 76–92), Recommendation 2 (Mathematical Language, printed pp. 11–20 / PDF pp. 18–27; evidence rationale, printed pp. 86–92 / PDF pp. 93–99), Recommendation 3 (Representations, printed pp. 21–28 / PDF pp. 28–35; evidence rationale, printed pp. 93–103 / PDF pp. 100–110), Recommendation 4 (Number Lines, printed pp. 29–39 / PDF pp. 36–46; evidence rationale, printed pp. 104–110 / PDF pp. 111–117), Recommendation 5 (Word Problems, printed pp. 40–50 / PDF pp. 47–57; evidence rationale, printed pp. 111–119 / PDF pp. 118–126), Recommendation 6 (Timed Activities, printed pp. 51–55 / PDF pp. 58–62; evidence rationale, printed pp. 120–130 / PDF pp. 127–137), Table C.1 Study Mapping (printed p. 65 / PDF p. 72)
references.researchRelevance: Serves as the foundational pedagogical evidence base for all MathQuest mathematics adaptations. High-quality research base: 56 eligible studies were reviewed; 44 unique studies met WWC group design standards (with or without reservations). Each of the 6 recommendations received a Strong level of evidence rating from the expert panel based on its supporting studies: Recommendation 1 is supported by 43 studies (32 without reservations, 11 with reservations); Recommendation 2 by 16 studies (12 without reservations, 4 with reservations); Recommendation 3 by 28 studies (19 without reservations, 9 with reservations); Recommendation 4 by 14 studies (11 without reservations, 3 with reservations); Recommendation 5 by 18 studies (15 without reservations, 3 with reservations); Recommendation 6 by 27 studies (21 without reservations, 6 with reservations). Individual studies evaluated multi-component packages and contributed to multiple recommendations (Table C.1). Guides the Concrete-Representational-Abstract (CRA) scaffolding progression, mathematical language framing, number lines, schema-based word problem categorization, and brief fluency activities.
references.limitations: Grounded in small-group and 1:1 human teacher-led Tier 2 interventions in US elementary schools (Grades K–6). Digital adaptations must translate teacher-led practices into automated software scaffolds. While the guide strongly supports instructional strategies conceptually, it does not specify software decision thresholds (e.g., exact trial counts or error thresholds). These thresholds require expert review and contextual calibration.
